question: Should OpenClaw permanently adopt the stricter base64/local-file boundary and publish `plugin-sdk/media-base64` as the supported plugin-facing contract for this WhatsApp refactor?
rationale: The branch is mechanically coherent, but the acceptable compatibility tradeoff and the permanent public SDK surface are product and security-boundary choices that cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Accept the shared boundary and facade
options.body: Approve the strict malformed-data-URL rejection, explicit local-root requirement, and focused SDK export as the supported cross-plugin contract.

options.title: Keep the refactor internal
options.body: Retain WhatsApp's canonical-path migration but avoid publishing the new SDK facade or broad Gateway behavior until a narrower owner-approved contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared boundary and facade
recommendation.body: Approve the strict malformed-data-URL rejection, explicit local-root requirement, and focused SDK export as the supported cross-plugin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified recent contributor for the proposed media, WhatsApp, and gateway changes and can provide the most direct technical context for the decision.
